newsitem.title: SPAIN: Siemens wants to join in Spanish train project.
newsitem.headline: Siemens wants to join in Spanish train project.

text.p: Siemens Espana SA, the Spanish subsidiary of Germany's Siemens AG, confirmed on Monday that it wants to participate in Spain's high-speed train project from Madrid to Barcelona.

A Siemens spokesman confirmed a report in local financial daily Cinco Dias that the group was interested in offering rolling stock, signalling, electrification, telecommunications and financing for the project.

The government is looking for private sector financing help for the project, but Siemens has a disadvantage in that it is in the midst of two court proceedings for payments of commissions, the spokesman said.

A Madrid court is studying the alleged payment of 972 million pesetas by Siemens in the Socialist Party financing scandal. In Pamplona, a court is looking into the alleged payment of a further 200 million pesetas to politicians in the Navarre region.
The spokesman said Siemens was in talks with various companies to form possible consortiums for the high-speed train project, but he declined to give any further details.

Siemens participated, along with other companies, in the high-speed train project between Madrid and Seville built early this decade. Its contribution was in electrification, signalisation and telecommunication.
